question: Which native entry carries each of the eleven checklist rows, and does the vanilla level-event payload really hold the information the author node needs?

answers.one-entry-for-eight-rows: Lights, fog, the repeating-fog pair, sound, intel, the nearest-player dialogue, the nav marker and the scene animation trigger are all members of `GameData.eWardenObjectiveEventType` on one `GameData.WardenObjectiveEventData`, and one static entry runs any of them: `WorldEventManager.ExecuteEvent(WardenObjectiveEventData, float)`. That is why this slice builds an event and hands it over instead of calling the effect's own manager: the type member selects the effect, the fields carry the arguments, and the game's own execution path does the replication it already does for its own data.
answers.sustained-pair-reached-through-the-same-: `AttemptTriggerSustainedEventMaster(WardenObjectiveEventData)` / `AttemptClearSustainedEventMaster(WardenObjectiveEventData)` are public statics, but they are the sustained-event arm of the same type switch `ExecuteEvent` reaches, and calling them directly would skip the condition and type gates the switch performs. The repeating-fog row therefore uses `ExecuteEvent` with `StartRepeatingFog` / `StopSustainedEvent`, which is also how vanilla data reaches the pair.
answers.intel-can-carry-free-text: `WardenObjectiveEventData.WardenIntel` is a `Localization.LocalizedText`, and `LocalizedText` has a public `(System.String)` constructor beside its `(System.UInt32)` one: the field is a text value with an optional localisation id, not an id-only key. A plan can therefore broadcast computed text such as a door's name or a live count, which is what the checklist's dynamic-text requirement asks for. The same constructor is what `a-sound`'s subtitle uses.
answers.two-zone-reads-are-state-not-events: The two environment facts are read from `EnvironmentStateManager`, the manager that owns both pieces of state and replicates them, rather than from a loop over the level's lights: `GetCurrentFogID(eDimensionIndex)` answers the dimension's fog block and `GetLightMode(GlobalZoneIndex)` answers one zone's mode.
answers.hud-writes-are-local: The local player's HUD is per machine: `GuiManager.Current.m_playerLayer.m_playerStatus` is the local status readout, its shield bar is written by `UpdateShield(float)`, its number field is `m_shieldText`, its group switch is `m_shieldUIParent`, and the text this slice clones for a screen readout comes from the same readout's `m_healthText`. A teammate's overhead line is per machine for the same reason: `PlayerAgent.NavMarker` is the marker that machine built, `NavMarker.m_playerName` is the mesh it clones, and the game re-renders it through `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.UpdateExtraInfo` — the member `InfiniTweaks.ResourceHud` already postfixes and this slice now does too. Nothing in either chain is replicated, which is why the row is a presentation capability and why the only per-player fact that travels is the number itself.
answers.one-session-per-player-is-the-networks-o: A player entity resolves to a session through the agent's own `Owner` and that player's `Lookup`, which is the value `NetworkCommandRouting.PresentationRequest` writes into a presentation request's endpoint slot and `IsPresentationRequest` compares with the local session. The handler therefore repeats the network layer's own comparison for `audience=self` instead of inventing a second address, and `a-p-say` reads the same player's `PlayerSlotIndex()` for the number the game's voice entry takes.
unverified: Whether `WorldEventManager.ExecuteEvent` called from a mod replicates exactly what the level's own call replicates for every one of the eight types. The manager is an `SNet_StateReplicatorProvider` and the effects (lights, fog, markers, animations) are its own replicated state, but the method bodies are stubs in this tree, so the claim rests on the type and field structure rather than on reading the call.

Whether `PlaySound` and `DialogueOnClosest` are meant to be executed on every client (this slice presents them locally) or only on the host. Vanilla's `DoExcecuteEvent` state machine carries a `localPlayer` field beside its `delay` and `success` locals, which is where the local-choice reading comes from; it is a weak signal, not a proven call graph.
`LightsInZone`'s meaning when `Position` and `Count` are absent: vanilla always sets both. The row passes them through when a plan supplies them and leaves the field defaults when it does not.

`PUI_LocalPlayerStatus.UpdateShield`'s real caller count (the interop xref says 2 on the status readout and 0 on the layer wrapper) and whether the shield bar's prefab is wired at all. The slice writes the game's own readout and clones the game's own text; whether the bar shows is a game-verification item.

`PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.UpdateExtraInfo` is the hook `InfiniTweaks.ResourceHud` already uses for a teammate overhead line, and this slice patches it too (`Native/TeammateOverheadHooks.cs`). Whether the game calls that member often enough to keep a per-teammate number current, and whether the native extra-information row's visibility can be taken over and given back without disturbing the game's own rescue and resource hints, are the two questions only a running game answers.

layoutAuditNote: The rows above are written in the same `Type::member(args)` spelling the alarm slice used. Three reads are non-getter members (EnvironmentStateManager.GetCurrentFogID, GetLightMode and SNet_Player.PlayerSlotIndex) and a getter-shaped rule files them under writes; they read state and write nothing. `PlaceNavMarkerOnGO.SetExtraInfoVisible` is written by this slice only through a Harmony prefix (the model assigns the field `m_extraInfoVisible` directly and never calls the method), and `UpdateExtraInfo`/`OnDestroy` are patch targets whose bodies this slice never calls. On the other side, the `GameData.WardenObjectiveEventData::get_*` rows exist because the events the slice builds are constructed and then read; the only members it actually sets are the ones its `members` rows mark as fields with a `usedBy` naming a row.
